title: Historical Plaster Cast Collection — RABASF
institution: Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando
shortDescription: Conservation and restoration of the historical plaster cast collection at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando. Project directly linked to the National Award 2004 and the Europa Nostra Award 2006.
longDescription: This project represents the defining work of Ángeles Solís Parra's career: the conservation and systematic restoration of the historical plaster cast collection at the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando. Works treated include the Ariadna, Crátera de Estabia, Flora Farnese, Puerta del Paraíso, Venus del Pomo and Venus Médici. The project required the development of a patented cleaning methodology — Anjusil® — specifically designed for the complex surface behavior of historical plaster casts.
sources: client-project-sheet — 6 works documented (Ariadna V-011, Crátera Estabia V-465, Flora Farnese V-002, Puerta del Paraíso, Venus del Pomo V-007, Venus Médici V-076): image roles only, no per-work date/material/intervention text provided by the client for these pieces

title: Premios y Envíos de Roma — RABASF Sculpture Collection
institution: Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando
shortDescription: Conservation of the Roma Prizes and Envíos collection at RABASF, including works by José Ginés (Apolino), Huberto Dumandré, Juan Adán and others.
longDescription: The Roma Prizes and Envíos collection represents the institutional memory of academic sculpture formation in Spain. Works treated include the Apolino de José Ginés (E-7), Andrés Atado a la Cruz de Huberto Dumandré (E-213), Marsias de Juan Adán (E-222), Santa Leocadia Azotada de Manuel Llorente (E-393), San Francisco de Paula de José Guerra (E-396) and El Rey Don Alonso el Casto de Santiago Rodríguez (E-501). Each piece required individual treatment protocols adapted to material history and institutional context.

title: Plaster Cast Collection — Universidad de Sevilla
shortDescription: Conservation of the historical plaster cast collection at the Universidad de Sevilla, applying the Anjusil® methodology developed at RABASF.
longDescription: Following the recognised work at RABASF, the University of Seville commissioned the conservation of its own plaster cast collection. This project extended the Anjusil® methodology to a different institutional and material context, consolidating its application beyond the original RABASF collection.

title: Museo Nacional de Reproducciones Artísticas
institution: Museo Nacional de Reproducciones Artísticas de Madrid
shortDescription: Conservation of the plaster cast and reproduction collection at the Museo Nacional de Reproducciones Artísticas de Madrid.
longDescription: The Museo Nacional de Reproducciones Artísticas holds one of Europe's most significant collections of artistic reproductions, including plaster casts, bronze and stone copies after major antique and Renaissance works. This conservation project involved assessment, stabilization and treatment of selected works from the permanent collection.

title: Archaeological Conservation — Pompeii
shortDescription: Conservation intervention at the Pompeii archaeological site, treating sculptural and architectural heritage in situ.
longDescription: International conservation work at the Pompeii archaeological site. Ángeles Solís Parra contributed to in-situ conservation of sculptural elements, working within the complex material and environmental conditions specific to the volcanic context and the demands of an active archaeological site.

title: Sculpture Conservation — Museo Nacional del Prado
shortDescription: Conservation of sculptural works from the collection of the Museo Nacional del Prado, under the Fundación Botín scholarship.
longDescription: Selected for the prestigious Fundación Botín scholarship at the Museo Nacional del Prado, Ángeles Solís Parra carried out conservation work on sculptural pieces from the Prado's permanent collection. This project represented a singular professional endorsement and the opportunity to work directly with one of the world's most important art collections.

title: Plateresque High Altar Retable (1538) — Berzosa de Bureba
shortDescription: Restoration of the plateresque high altar retable (1538) at the Iglesia de la Asunción de Nuestra Señora, Berzosa de Bureba, in gilded and polychrome wood.
longDescription: The restoration of the high altar retable was carried out in 1990 with the company Kipsa. The ensemble, made of gilded and polychrome wood, presented significant structural damage as well as deterioration of its sculptural group. The intervention included general cleaning, consolidation of the polychromy, material consolidation, fungicidal treatments and chromatic reintegration, aiming to stabilise the piece and recover its aesthetic and historic-artistic legibility.

title: Baroque High Altar Retable (1628–34) — Grandas de Salime
institution: Facultad de Bellas Artes, Universidad Complutense de Madrid
shortDescription: Restoration of the baroque high altar retable (1628–34) at the Colegiata de El Salvador, Grandas de Salime, including structural remounting and polychromy conservation.
longDescription: The restoration of the high altar retable was carried out in 1993 at the Faculty of Fine Arts of the Universidad Complutense de Madrid. The ensemble, made of gilded and polychrome wood, presented deterioration affecting both its structure and its sculptural group. The intervention included mounting and anchoring the retable structure to the wall, carpentry work, general cleaning, polychromy consolidation, material consolidation, fungicidal treatments and volumetric and chromatic reintegration. In 1993 the town received the Premio al Pueblo Ejemplar de Asturias, among other reasons for the rehabilitation of the Romanesque Colegiata de El Salvador, including this retable.

title: Baroque High Altar Retable (1666) — Medina de Rioseco
shortDescription: Restoration of the dismantled baroque high altar retable (1666) at the Iglesia-Museo de la Santa Cruz, Medina de Rioseco.
longDescription: The restoration of the high altar retable was carried out in 1991 with the company Kipsa. The ensemble, made of gilded and polychrome wood, was found dismantled, posing a significant structural intervention challenge. The work focused on restoring and remounting the retable structure, together with general cleaning, polychromy consolidation, material consolidation, fungicidal treatments and volumetric and chromatic reintegration, aiming to recover its stability and historic-artistic legibility.

title: Baroque Altar Retable of Saint Joseph (1707) — San Juan de la Rambla
location: San Juan de la Rambla, Tenerife, Spain
shortDescription: Restoration of the baroque altar retable of Saint Joseph (1707) at the Iglesia de San Juan de la Rambla, Tenerife.
longDescription: The restoration of the altar retable of Saint Joseph was carried out in 1995 for the Cabildo de Tenerife. The ensemble, made of gilded and polychrome wood, presented structural alterations and surface conservation problems. The intervention included general cleaning, polychromy consolidation, material consolidation, fungicidal treatments and volumetric and chromatic reintegration, aiming to stabilise the piece and recover its historic-artistic legibility.

title: Sculptural Ensemble — Cúpula de San Andrés
shortDescription: Conservation of the sculptural ensemble of the Cúpula de San Andrés in Madrid.
longDescription: Conservation of the sculptural programme associated with the dome of San Andrés church in Madrid, a significant baroque heritage ensemble. Work involved structural consolidation, surface cleaning and chromatic integration of sculptural elements within an active ecclesiastical building.

title: Painting Conservation — RABASF Collection
institution: Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando
shortDescription: Conservation and restoration of paintings from the permanent collection of the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando, including works by Alonso Cano and Van Dyck.
longDescription: Over a decade of sustained work on the painting collection of the Real Academia de Bellas Artes de San Fernando. Works treated include La Muerte de San Francisco de Asís by Alonso Cano (inv. 553) and a painting attributed to Van Dyck, as well as numerous other works from the permanent collection. Conservation criteria prioritised material integrity, chromatic coherence and institutional accountability.

title: Painting Conservation — Museo de Bellas Artes de Málaga
institution: Museo de Bellas Artes de Málaga
shortDescription: Conservation of paintings from the Museo de Bellas Artes de Málaga, including works by Nogales and Denis Belgrano.
longDescription: Conservation project for the Museo de Bellas Artes de Málaga, treating works of significant regional heritage value including paintings by Nogales and Pato Denis Belgrano. The project required adaptation of conservation criteria to works with complex varnish histories and previous interventions.

title: Painting Conservation — Museo de Bellas Artes de Granada
institution: Museo de Bellas Artes de Granada
shortDescription: Extensive conservation project for the Museo de Bellas Artes de Granada, involving multiple canvas paintings with complex structural and surface interventions.
longDescription: One of the most extensive painting conservation projects in Ángeles Solís Parra's practice, involving multiple large-format canvas works from the permanent collection of the Museo de Bellas Artes de Granada. Interventions addressed canvas support, ground layer, paint film and varnish for a series of works with layered conservation histories.

title: Archaeological Mural — Museo-Yacimiento de Campo Valdés
shortDescription: Conservation of mural painting fragments within the archaeological museum-site of Campo Valdés in Gijón.
longDescription: In-situ conservation of Roman mural painting fragments within the Campo Valdés archaeological site in Gijón, a significant bath complex from Roman Hispania. Work required adaptation to the archaeological context and the specific material behavior of fragmentary wall painting.

title: Mural Painting — Casa de Diezmos, Somosierra
shortDescription: Conservation of mural painting in the historic Casa de Diezmos in Somosierra, Madrid.
longDescription: Conservation of interior mural paintings in the Casa de Diezmos in Somosierra, a historic building associated with ecclesiastical land management. The intervention addressed structural support, surface cleaning and consolidation of figurative and decorative mural schemes.

title: Mural Painting — Capilla del Cardenal, Catedral de Zamora
shortDescription: Conservation of the mural painting cycle in the Capilla del Cardenal at the Cathedral of Zamora.
longDescription: Conservation of medieval mural paintings in the Capilla del Cardenal at the Cathedral of Zamora, a building of major architectural and heritage significance. The project involved preventive consolidation, cleaning and chromatic reintegration of a multi-layered mural programme.

title: Private Collections — Esperanza Parada & José Nogué Massó
shortDescription: Conservation of easel paintings from private collections, including works from the collection of the artist Esperanza Parada and works attributed to José Nogué Massó.
longDescription: A sustained programme of conservation work for private collectors, requiring the discretion, technical precision and personal trust specific to private collection practice. Works include multiple still-life paintings by Esperanza Parada (Bodegones) and paintings from the estate of José Nogué Massó, the Spanish landscape painter.

title: Anjusil® — Patented Conservation Methodology
shortDescription: Development, testing and patenting of Anjusil®, a specialised cleaning methodology for historical plaster cast collections. Connected to the National Award 2004 and Europa Nostra Award 2006.
longDescription: Anjusil® is the patented conservation methodology developed by Ángeles Solís Parra during the restoration of the RABASF plaster cast collection. The methodology addresses the specific challenges of cleaning historical plaster casts: the porosity of the material, the surface accumulation of dust, soiling and biological growth, and the need to preserve evidence of historical handling and aging without aggressive intervention. The development process involved material testing, chemical analysis and documentation across multiple cast typologies.

title: National Award 2004 & Europa Nostra 2006
shortDescription: National Award for Conservation and Restoration of Cultural Heritage (2004, Ministry of Culture) and Europa Nostra Award (2006), both connected to the recovery of the historical plaster cast collections.
longDescription: In 2004, Ángeles Solís Parra received the National Award for Conservation and Restoration of Cultural Heritage from the Spanish Ministry of Culture, in recognition of the work carried out on the historical plaster cast collection at RABASF. In 2006, the same project was recognised with the Europa Nostra Award, the most prestigious European prize for cultural heritage practice. These recognitions confirm the professional and institutional significance of the work and the Anjusil® methodology at European level.
